title: Fix workflow test YAML on-key parsing and epic design text
description: Two related cleanup items: (1) workflow.test.ts:22 uses workflow.on || workflow.true || {} - the YAML parser converts unquoted 'on' key to boolean true, so workflow['on'] is undefined but workflow[true] has the data. Use explicit bracket notation workflow['on'] to make intent clear. (2) Epic pages-994 Requirements say 'push to main + workflow_dispatch' but Anti-Patterns says 'NO auto-deploy triggers'. Actual code is workflow_dispatch only. Update epic text to be consistent.
design:
## Goal
Clean up two inconsistencies: (1) remove dead code fallback in workflow test, (2) fix contradictory text in epic design.

## Effort Estimate
~30 minutes

## Implementation Checklist
- [ ] In tests/workflow.test.ts line 22, simplify the trigger extraction:
      BEFORE: const triggers = Object.keys(workflow.on || workflow.true || {});
      AFTER:  const triggers = Object.keys(workflow.on || {});
      Rationale: The yaml npm package (v2.8.2) uses YAML 1.2 which parses 'on' as string "on", not boolean true. Verified: workflow.on returns the correct object, workflow[true] is undefined. The workflow.true fallback is dead code.
- [ ] Update epic pages-994 Requirements to be consistent with actual implementation:
      Run: bd update pages-994 --notes "Requirements text updated: 'push to main + workflow_dispatch triggers' changed to 'workflow_dispatch trigger only' to match actual implementation and Anti-Patterns section."
      Then update the design field to change the one line:
      BEFORE: - Single workflow: push to main + workflow_dispatch triggers
      AFTER:  - Single workflow: workflow_dispatch trigger only
- [ ] Run bun test and verify all tests pass

## Success Criteria
- [ ] workflow.test.ts line 22 no longer references workflow.true
- [ ] Epic pages-994 Requirements section says "workflow_dispatch trigger only"
- [ ] Epic Requirements and Anti-Patterns sections are consistent (both say manual-only)
- [ ] All tests pass (bun test)

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**YAML Parsing Verification** (already done):
- Tested with bun -e: yaml package v2.8.2 parses 'on' as string key "on"
- workflow.on correctly returns { workflow_dispatch: null }
- workflow[true] returns undefined (dead code path)
- The || {} fallback is still useful as a safety net if the key is missing entirely

**Epic Text Scope**:
- Only change the one contradictory line in Requirements
- Do NOT touch Anti-Patterns section (it's already correct)
- Do NOT change any other design text (immutable requirements otherwise)

## Anti-patterns
- Do NOT add YAML 1.1 compatibility handling (we control the parser version via package.json)
- Do NOT change the test logic beyond removing the dead fallback (test is otherwise correct)

title: Personal site: Astro root + Starlight docs pipeline
design:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Astro site deployed to sethyanow.github.io root (/)
- Three pages: Home (landing/hero), About (portfolio/resume), Projects (showcase with links)
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- bun as package manager (local and CI)
- GitHub Actions workflow builds root Astro site + clones/builds markymark Starlight docs
- markymark docs accessible at sethyanow.github.io/markymark/
- Single workflow: push to main + workflow_dispatch triggers
- GitHub Pages source set to GitHub Actions

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] Astro site builds successfully with bun
- [ ] Home, About, Projects pages render with proper navigation
- [ ] Tailwind styles applied correctly
- [ ] GitHub Actions workflow succeeds end-to-end
- [ ] Root site accessible at sethyanow.github.io/
- [ ] markymark docs accessible at sethyanow.github.io/markymark/
- [ ] All internal links work (no broken paths)
- [ ] Site is responsive (mobile-friendly)

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- NO npm/yarn/pnpm (consistency: bun is the standard per user preferences)
- NO blog in phase 1 (YAGNI: deferred to next phase by explicit decision)
- NO auto-deploy triggers (YAGNI: manual workflow_dispatch only for now)
- NO git submodules (complexity: painful in CI, checkout-in-workflow is simpler)
- NO base path on root Astro site (correctness: username.github.io deploys to /, no base needed)
- NO unified build for project docs (architecture: separate Starlight builds per project, assembled at deploy time)
- NO starter templates or themes (user wants custom from scratch)
- NO HTML for basic content (preference: Markdown where possible)

## Approach
Custom Astro site with Tailwind CSS, built with bun. Root site has Home, About, and Projects pages with shared Layout component. GitHub Actions workflow builds the root site, then clones and builds markymark Starlight docs (which set base: '/markymark' in their own astro.config), then assembles both into _site/ directory and deploys to GitHub Pages.

## Architecture
- src/layouts/Layout.astro - Base layout with head, header, footer
- src/pages/index.astro - Home page with hero
- src/pages/about.astro - About/resume page
- src/pages/projects.astro - Project showcase
- src/components/ - Header, Footer, Hero, ProjectCard
- src/styles/global.css - Tailwind directives
- astro.config.mjs - Astro config with Tailwind integration
- .github/workflows/deploy.yml - Build + assemble + deploy

Actions workflow structure:
1. Checkout this repo
2. Checkout markymark repo into _projects/markymark
3. Setup bun
4. Build root Astro site (output: dist/)
5. Build markymark Starlight docs (output: _projects/markymark/dist/)
6. Assemble: cp dist/* _site/ && mv _projects/markymark/dist _site/markymark
7. Upload + deploy to GitHub Pages

## Design Rationale
### Problem
Need a personal homepage at sethyanow.github.io that serves as both a portfolio/resume site and a hub for project documentation (starting with markymark).

### Research Findings
**External (user's Perplexity research):**
- Astro Starlight docs can deploy to subpaths with base config
- Hub repo pattern: checkout + build + assemble in Actions
- upload-pages-artifact@v3 + deploy-pages@v4 is the current GitHub Pages deploy pattern
- base path in Starlight astro.config must match the subdir name in _site/

### Approaches Considered

#### 1. Single workflow, assemble at build time (CHOSEN)
**What it is:** One Actions workflow in this repo handles everything - builds root site, clones + builds each project's docs, assembles into _site/, deploys.

**Pros:**
- Simple to reason about - one workflow, one deploy
- Easy to add projects (copy checkout+build+copy block)
- Atomic deploys (everything updates together)

**Cons:**
- Rebuild everything even if only one project changed
- Build time grows with projects

**Chosen because:** Simple, correct, sufficient for 1-3 projects. Optimize later if needed.

#### 2. Separate workflows per project
**What it is:** Each project repo deploys its own docs independently.

**Why we looked at this:** More decoupled, each project owns its deploy.

**Pros:** Independent deploys, less rebuild waste
**Cons:** Partial deploy risk, complex coordination, Pages can only have one source

**REJECTED BECAUSE:** GitHub Pages only supports one deploy source per repo. Separate deploys would overwrite each other.

**DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** GitHub Pages supports multiple deploy sources (unlikely).

#### 3. Git submodules
**What it is:** Add project repos as git submodules.

**Why we looked at this:** Avoids clone-in-CI pattern.

**Pros:** Version-pinned, familiar git concept
**Cons:** Submodules are painful to maintain, CI caching harder

**REJECTED BECAUSE:** Complexity cost not worth it for a personal site. Checkout-in-workflow is simpler.

**DO NOT REVISIT UNLESS:** Managing 10+ project repos and need version pinning.

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:**
- Astro root site (Home, About, Projects)
- Tailwind CSS styling
- GitHub Actions workflow for build + deploy
- markymark Starlight docs integration

**Out of scope (deferred):**
- Blog (phase 2)
- Auto-deploy via repository_dispatch (add when manual gets annoying)
- Additional project docs beyond markymark (pattern established, add as needed)
- Custom domain (use GitHub default for now)

### Open Questions
- GitHub repo path for markymark (need org/repo for Actions checkout)
- markymark Starlight docs: confirm base path is set to '/markymark'
- Content for About/resume page (placeholder or real content in phase 1?)

## Design Discovery (Reference Context)

### Key Decisions Made

| Question | User Answer | Implication |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Site purpose? | Full personal homepage + docs hosting | Need proper pages, not just docs index |
| Framework? | Astro | Static-first, islands architecture |
| Docs strategy? | Hybrid (Astro root + separate Starlight builds) | Actions assembles at deploy time |
| Design approach? | Custom from scratch | No starter templates |
| CSS? | Tailwind CSS | @astrojs/tailwind integration |
| Build order? | Both together | Root site + docs pipeline in one epic |
| Pages? | Home + About + Projects | Three-page site |
| Package manager? | bun | Everywhere including CI |
| Markymark docs? | Being set up in parallel | Just need to wire up the checkout+build |
| Auto-deploy? | Manual only for now | workflow_dispatch, no repository_dispatch |
| Blog? | Next phase | YAGNI for phase 1 |
notes:
RESOLVED open questions:
- GitHub repo path: sethyanow/markymark (confirmed public)
- markymark base path: confirmed '/markymark' in astro.config.prod.mjs
- About page content: placeholder for phase 1 (confirmed by user in brainstorming)
- Build command: bun run build:prod in docs-site/ subdirectory

title: Scaffold Astro project with Tailwind and basic page structure
description: Set up the Astro project in this repo with bun, Tailwind CSS, and the three initial pages (Home, About, Projects). Create the component structure (Layout, Header, Footer, Hero, ProjectCard). Verify it builds and dev server works locally.
design:
## Goal
Scaffold the Astro project with Tailwind CSS, create the page and component structure, verify it builds with bun. This task produces a working local dev site with all three pages navigable.

## Effort Estimate
4-6 hours

## Implementation Checklist

### 1. Initialize Astro project
- Run `bun create astro@latest` in repo root (select empty/minimal template, NOT a starter theme)
- OR manually: create package.json, install astro + dependencies with bun
- Ensure bun.lock is created (NOT package-lock.json or yarn.lock)
- Configure astro.config.mjs:
  ```js
  site: "https://sethyanow.github.io"  // no trailing slash
  ```
- Existing files (README.md, AGENTS.md, .beads/, temp/) must coexist — do NOT delete them
- Add appropriate entries to .gitignore (node_modules, dist, .astro)

### 2. Set up Tailwind CSS
- Astro 5.x: check if @astrojs/tailwind supports Tailwind v4, or if we need @tailwindcss/vite as a Vite plugin
- If Tailwind v4: add @tailwindcss/vite to astro.config.mjs vite.plugins, import tailwindcss in global.css
- If Tailwind v3: use @astrojs/tailwind integration
- Create src/styles/global.css with Tailwind directives
- Verify: a Tailwind utility class (e.g., `text-blue-500`) renders correctly in browser

### 3. Create base layout
- src/layouts/Layout.astro
  - HTML5 docstring, lang="en"
  - <head> with meta charset, viewport, title prop, global.css import
  - <body> wraps <Header />, <slot />, <Footer />
  - Props: title (string), description (string, optional)

### 4. Create components
- src/components/Header.astro
  - Site name/logo text linking to /
  - Nav links: Home (/), About (/about), Projects (/projects)
  - Responsive: hamburger/collapse on mobile (can be CSS-only, no JS required)
- src/components/Footer.astro
  - Copyright line, GitHub link
- src/components/Hero.astro
  - Heading, subtitle text, optional CTA button
  - Props: heading (string), subtitle (string)
- src/components/ProjectCard.astro
  - Props: name (string), description (string), url (string), tags (string[], optional)
  - Renders: card with name, description, link, optional tag badges

### 5. Create pages
- src/pages/index.astro — Home
  - Hero component with name + tagline
  - Brief intro section
  - Uses Layout with title="Home"
- src/pages/about.astro — About
  - Placeholder content for now (heading + a few paragraphs)
  - Uses Layout with title="About"
- src/pages/projects.astro — Projects
  - At least one ProjectCard for markymark:
    - name: "markymark"
    - description: "Markdown workspace indexer with LSP and MCP support"
    - url: "/markymark/" (will link to Starlight docs once pipeline is set up)
  - Uses Layout with title="Projects"

### 6. Verify
- `bun run dev` — dev server starts without errors
- Visit http://localhost:4321/ — home page renders with Hero
- Visit http://localhost:4321/about — about page renders
- Visit http://localhost:4321/projects — projects page renders with markymark card
- Click nav links — all three pages navigable
- `bun run build` — produces dist/ directory without errors or warnings
- Check dist/ contains: index.html, about/index.html, projects/index.html

## Success Criteria
- [ ] `bun run build` completes with exit code 0 and zero warnings
- [ ] dist/ contains index.html, about/index.html, projects/index.html
- [ ] All three pages render in browser with visible Tailwind-styled content (verify at least one utility class renders, e.g., colored text or spacing)
- [ ] Header nav links navigate between all three pages (/, /about, /projects)
- [ ] Layout component used by all pages (verified: all pages import Layout)
- [ ] ProjectCard renders markymark entry on /projects with name, description, and link
- [ ] Site is responsive: header collapses or adapts on narrow viewport (~375px)
- [ ] No package-lock.json, yarn.lock, or pnpm-lock.yaml created (bun only)

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Tailwind v3 vs v4:**
- Astro 5.x officially supports both, but integration method differs
- @astrojs/tailwind is for v3. Tailwind v4 uses @tailwindcss/vite as Vite plugin
- Check Astro docs at build time — install whichever is current stable
- If unsure: Tailwind v3 + @astrojs/tailwind is the safe, well-documented path

**Site config — no trailing slash:**
- site must be "https://sethyanow.github.io" (no trailing slash)
- Trailing slash causes double-slash in generated URLs
- Astro trailingSlash option defaults to "ignore" — leave default for now

**Coexistence with existing files:**
- Repo already has: README.md, AGENTS.md, .beads/, .gitignore, temp/
- Astro scaffolding must not delete or overwrite these
- If using `bun create astro`, it may want a clean directory — may need manual init instead

**Production build output format:**
- Astro generates /about/index.html for /about routes by default (directory-style)
- This is correct for GitHub Pages — do not change

## Anti-Patterns (from epic, relevant to this task)
- NO npm/yarn/pnpm — bun only, verify no non-bun lock files created
- NO starter templates or themes — empty/minimal template only, custom components
- NO base path — this is username.github.io, deploys to root
close_reason: Astro 5.18 + Tailwind v4 scaffolded. All 3 pages build, nav works, responsive header, markymark ProjectCard, 12 build tests passing.

title: Fix markymark docs build: checkout needs ref docs-site branch
description: The deploy workflow checks out sethyanow/markymark at default branch (main), but the docs-site/ directory only exists on the docs-site branch. Steps 'Install markymark docs dependencies' and 'Build markymark docs' with working-directory _projects/markymark/docs-site will fail. Fix: add ref: docs-site to the markymark checkout step. Also fix assembly step to use cp -r dist/. _site/ (dotfile-safe) and add set -e with directory existence checks.
design:
## Goal
Fix the deploy workflow so markymark docs actually build. Currently the workflow checks out markymark's main branch, but docs-site/ only exists on the docs-site branch. Also fix dotfile-unsafe cp and add assembly validation.

## Effort Estimate
~2 hours

## Implementation Checklist
- [ ] In .github/workflows/deploy.yml line 24-28, add ref: docs-site to markymark checkout:
      - name: Checkout markymark
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: sethyanow/markymark
          ref: docs-site
          path: _projects/markymark
- [ ] In .github/workflows/deploy.yml lines 47-51, replace assembly step with validated, dotfile-safe version:
      - name: Assemble _site
        run: |
          set -e
          test -d dist || { echo 'Error: root dist/ not found'; exit 1; }
          test -d _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist || { echo 'Error: markymark docs-site/dist not found'; exit 1; }
          mkdir _site
          cp -r dist/. _site/
          mv _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist _site/markymark
- [ ] Update tests/workflow.test.ts to verify ref: docs-site is present:
      test('checks out markymark docs-site branch', () => {
        const yaml = JSON.stringify(workflow);
        expect(yaml).toContain('"ref":"docs-site"');
      });
- [ ] Run bun test and verify all tests pass (including new test)
- [ ] Verify with bun run build that root site still builds

## Success Criteria
- [ ] deploy.yml markymark checkout step has ref: docs-site
- [ ] Assembly step uses set -e and validates both dist directories exist
- [ ] Assembly uses cp -r dist/. (dotfile-safe) instead of cp -r dist/*
- [ ] New test 'checks out markymark docs-site branch' passes
- [ ] All existing 22 tests still pass (bun test shows 22 pass)
- [ ] Root site builds cleanly (bun run build exits 0)

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Branch Stability**:
- docs-site branch must exist in sethyanow/markymark at deploy time
- If branch is deleted/renamed, workflow fails with clear checkout error
- This is acceptable: branch deletion is a deliberate action, not an accident

**Build Script Verification** (confirmed):
- docs-site/package.json has "build:prod": "astro build --config astro.config.prod.mjs"
- astro.config.prod.mjs sets base: '/markymark' and site: 'https://sethyanow.github.io'
- Output directory is dist/ (Astro default)
- All paths in the workflow are correct AFTER the ref fix

**Dotfile Handling**:
- cp -r dist/* skips dotfiles like .nojekyll (needed for GitHub Pages to serve _-prefixed paths)
- cp -r dist/. copies everything including dotfiles
- Astro doesn't currently generate .nojekyll but future versions or plugins might

**Assembly Validation**:
- set -e ensures any command failure stops the step
- test -d checks prevent cryptic 'cp: No such file or directory' errors
- Error messages name the missing directory for quick diagnosis

## Anti-patterns
- Do NOT use cp -r dist/* (skips dotfiles)
- Do NOT omit ref: from markymark checkout (defaults to main which lacks docs-site/)
- Do NOT remove the set -e or directory checks (they prevent silent failures)

title: Split deploy workflow into build and deploy jobs for credential scoping
description: Currently pages:write and id-token:write permissions are granted to the build job which also runs bun install and builds code from external repo (sethyanow/markymark). A compromised dependency could abuse these credentials. Split into: (1) build job with contents:read only that builds both sites and uploads artifact, (2) deploy job with pages:write and id-token:write that only deploys the artifact. Uses needs: [build] dependency.
design:
## Goal
Split the single build job into two jobs (build + deploy) so that elevated Pages credentials (pages:write, id-token:write) are only available to the deploy step, not to steps that run bun install and build code from an external repository.

## Effort Estimate
~2 hours

## Implementation Checklist
- [ ] In .github/workflows/deploy.yml, split the current 'build' job into two jobs:

  **Job 1: build** (runs untrusted code with minimal permissions)
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          contents: read
        steps:
          - name: Checkout site
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - name: Checkout markymark
            uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              repository: sethyanow/markymark
              ref: docs-site
              path: _projects/markymark
          - name: Setup Bun
            uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
          - name: Install root dependencies
            run: bun install
          - name: Build root site
            run: bun run build
          - name: Install markymark docs dependencies
            run: bun install
            working-directory: _projects/markymark/docs-site
          - name: Build markymark docs
            run: bun run build:prod
            working-directory: _projects/markymark/docs-site
          - name: Assemble _site
            run: |
              set -e
              test -d dist || { echo 'Error: root dist/ not found'; exit 1; }
              test -d _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist || { echo 'Error: markymark docs-site/dist not found'; exit 1; }
              mkdir _site
              cp -r dist/. _site/
              mv _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist _site/markymark
          - name: Upload artifact
            uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
            with:
              path: _site

  **Job 2: deploy** (only has Pages credentials, no code execution)
      deploy:
        needs: build
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          pages: write
          id-token: write
        environment:
          name: github-pages
          url: \${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
        steps:
          - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
            id: deployment
            uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

- [ ] Move concurrency to workflow level (already there) and keep cancel-in-progress: false
- [ ] Update tests/workflow.test.ts to verify two-job structure:
      test('has separate build and deploy jobs', () => {
        expect(workflow.jobs.build).toBeDefined();
        expect(workflow.jobs.deploy).toBeDefined();
      });
      test('deploy job depends on build job', () => {
        expect(workflow.jobs.deploy.needs).toContain('build');
      });
      test('build job has only contents:read permission', () => {
        expect(workflow.jobs.build.permissions).toEqual({ contents: 'read' });
      });
      test('deploy job has pages:write and id-token:write', () => {
        expect(workflow.jobs.deploy.permissions?.pages).toBe('write');
        expect(workflow.jobs.deploy.permissions?.['id-token']).toBe('write');
      });
- [ ] Remove or update the old 'has required permissions' test (line 37-42) since permissions are now split across jobs
- [ ] Run bun test and verify all tests pass
- [ ] Verify workflow YAML is valid: bun -e "const {parse} = require('yaml'); parse(await Bun.file('.github/workflows/deploy.yml').text()); console.log('Valid YAML')"

## Success Criteria
- [ ] deploy.yml has two jobs: build and deploy
- [ ] build job permissions: only contents: read
- [ ] deploy job permissions: pages: write and id-token: write
- [ ] deploy job has needs: [build]
- [ ] environment block is on deploy job (not build)
- [ ] All new tests pass verifying job structure, permissions, dependencies
- [ ] All existing tests still pass (may need updates for two-job structure)
- [ ] YAML parses without errors

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Credential Scoping Rationale**:
- Build job runs bun install against both this repo and markymark
- bun install executes postinstall scripts from dependencies
- A compromised dependency in markymark could exfiltrate Pages write token or mint OIDC tokens
- After split: build job can only read (contents: read), deploy job never runs user code

**Artifact Passing**:
- upload-pages-artifact@v3 in build job creates the artifact
- deploy-pages@v4 in deploy job consumes it
- This is the standard GitHub Pages pattern; no additional download step needed
- deploy-pages automatically finds the artifact uploaded by upload-pages-artifact

**Test Migration**:
- The existing 'has required permissions' test checks for pages:write and id-token:write on the build job
- This test must be updated: build job should NOT have those permissions anymore
- New tests verify permissions are correctly split between jobs

**Edge Case: Build Failure**:
- If build job fails, deploy job never runs (needs: [build] ensures this)
- No partial deploy risk

## Anti-patterns
- Do NOT put pages:write on the build job (defeats the security purpose)
- Do NOT use a shared permissions block at workflow level (would apply to all jobs)
- Do NOT use actions/download-artifact in deploy job (deploy-pages handles this)
- Do NOT remove the environment block from the deploy job (required for Pages deployments)

title: Create GitHub Actions deploy workflow
description: Create .github/workflows/deploy.yml that builds root Astro site, clones/builds markymark Starlight docs, assembles into _site/, and deploys to GitHub Pages. Uses bun, workflow_dispatch trigger only, upload-pages-artifact@v3 + deploy-pages@v4 pattern.
design:
## Goal
Create the GitHub Actions workflow that builds the root Astro site, clones and builds markymark Starlight docs, assembles both into a single _site/ directory, and deploys to GitHub Pages.

## Effort Estimate
2-4 hours

## Context
- Root Astro site (pages-c7v) is complete and builds with \`bun run build\` producing dist/
- markymark Starlight docs are in sethyanow/markymark repo under docs-site/ subdirectory
- markymark docs use \`bun run build:prod\` which sets base: '/markymark' via astro.config.prod.mjs
- markymark repo is public (no PAT needed for checkout)

## Implementation Checklist

### 1. Create workflow file
- Create .github/workflows/deploy.yml
- Trigger: workflow_dispatch only (NO push, NO pull_request)
- Permissions at job level: pages: write, id-token: write, contents: read
- Concurrency group: pages (cancel-in-progress: false to prevent partial deploys)
- runs-on: ubuntu-latest

### 2. Workflow steps (in order)
1. Checkout this repo: actions/checkout@v4
2. Checkout markymark: actions/checkout@v4 with repository: sethyanow/markymark, path: _projects/markymark
3. Setup bun: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
4. Install root deps: \`bun install\`
5. Build root site: \`bun run build\` (produces dist/)
6. Install markymark docs deps: \`bun install\` with working-directory: _projects/markymark/docs-site
7. Build markymark docs: \`bun run build:prod\` with working-directory: _projects/markymark/docs-site (produces _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist/)
8. Assemble _site/:
   \`\`\`bash
   mkdir _site
   cp -r dist/* _site/
   mv _projects/markymark/docs-site/dist _site/markymark
   \`\`\`
9. Upload: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3, path: _site
10. Deploy: actions/deploy-pages@v4, id: deployment

### 3. Environment block
- environment: name: github-pages, url: \${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
- The deploy step MUST have id: deployment for the URL output to work

### 4. Write workflow structure test
- Add test in tests/workflow.test.ts that parses the YAML and verifies:
  - Only trigger is workflow_dispatch (no push, no pull_request)
  - Uses oven-sh/setup-bun (not actions/setup-node)
  - References sethyanow/markymark repository
  - Has pages: write and id-token: write permissions
  - Uses upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages actions
  - Assembly step creates _site/markymark path

### 5. Manual prerequisite (document, don't automate)
- GitHub Pages source must be set to "GitHub Actions" in repo Settings > Pages
- This is a one-time manual step, NOT part of the workflow
- Document in commit message or epic notes

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Workflow YAML passes validation: \`bun add -d yaml && bun -e "import {parse} from 'yaml'; parse(await Bun.file('.github/workflows/deploy.yml').text())"\`
- [ ] workflow_dispatch is the ONLY trigger (no push, no pull_request, no schedule)
- [ ] No npm/node/npx commands in any step (bun only)
- [ ] markymark checkout uses repository: sethyanow/markymark
- [ ] markymark build uses working-directory: _projects/markymark/docs-site with build:prod script
- [ ] Assembly creates _site/ with root site files and _site/markymark/ with docs
- [ ] Uses upload-pages-artifact@v3 and deploy-pages@v4
- [ ] Job permissions: pages: write, id-token: write, contents: read
- [ ] Concurrency group prevents overlapping deploys
- [ ] Deploy step has id: deployment for URL output
- [ ] tests/workflow.test.ts verifies workflow structure (6+ assertions)
- [ ] \`bun test\` passes (both existing build tests and new workflow test)

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Concurrency control:**
- Multiple workflow_dispatch runs could overlap
- Use concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: false
- false (not true) because canceling mid-deploy could leave Pages in partial state

**GitHub Pages source configuration:**
- The repo MUST have Pages source set to "GitHub Actions" (not "Deploy from a branch")
- This is a manual one-time step in Settings > Pages
- Workflow will fail with permission error if not configured

**markymark build failure:**
- If markymark docs-site build fails, the entire workflow fails (default GHA behavior)
- This is correct - we want atomic deploys, not partial ones
- If markymark repo structure changes, this workflow will break and need updating

**Assembly step edge cases:**
- \`cp -r dist/*\` won't copy dot-files from dist/ - this is fine for Astro output
- \`mv\` (not \`cp\`) for markymark dist ensures no duplicate data in artifact
- _site/ is freshly created each run, no stale content risk

**Action version pinning:**
- Using @v4/@v3/@v2 major version tags (not SHA pins)
- Acceptable for a personal site; SHA pinning is overkill here
- If supply chain concern arises later, pin to full SHA

## Anti-Patterns
- NO push trigger (epic anti-pattern: manual only via workflow_dispatch)
- NO npm/npx/node commands (bun exclusively, per user stack preferences)
- NO PAT or secrets for markymark checkout (repo is public)
- NO continue-on-error on build steps (partial deploys are worse than failed deploys)
- NO cancel-in-progress: true (could leave Pages in partial state)
- NO actions/setup-node (use oven-sh/setup-bun)

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Gitignore Paths**:
- _projects/ is created by the deploy workflow (checkout markymark into it)
- _site/ is created by the assembly step

- Adding them prevents accidental git add -A including large build artifacts

**Regex Assertion**:
- /class="[^"]*\bmin-h-screen\b/ matches min-h-screen anywhere within a class="" attribute
- Word boundary \b ensures we don't match "xmin-h-screen" or "min-h-screeny"

title: Accessibility and UX fixes for Header component
description: Two findings in Header.astro: (1) Line 23: SVG hamburger icon missing aria-hidden=true - it's decorative since the label has aria-label='Toggle navigation'. (2) Line 26: Mobile menu has no close-on-outside-click. Add a CSS-only overlay label that covers the viewport when menu is open, clicking it unchecks the toggle. Both are CSS/HTML only changes, no JS needed.
design:
## Goal
Fix two accessibility/UX issues in Header.astro: add aria-hidden to decorative SVG, add CSS-only overlay to close mobile menu on outside click.

## Effort Estimate
~1 hour

## Implementation Checklist
- [ ] In src/components/Header.astro line 23, add aria-hidden="true" to SVG:
      <svg class="w-6 h-6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">
- [ ] After the closing </label> on line 26, add a backdrop overlay label:
      <label
        for="nav-toggle"
        class="fixed inset-0 bg-black/20 hidden peer-checked:block md:hidden z-10"
        aria-hidden="true"
      ></label>
- [ ] Ensure the nav ul has z-20 or higher so it renders above the overlay:
      Add z-20 to the ul class list on line 28
- [ ] Update tests/build.test.ts 'responsive header markup present' test to verify:
      test('responsive header markup present', async () => {
        const html = await Bun.file(join(distDir, 'index.html')).text();
        expect(html).toContain('md:hidden');
        expect(html).toContain('md:flex');
        expect(html).toContain('aria-hidden="true"');
      });
- [ ] Run bun test and verify all tests pass
- [ ] Manual check: bun run dev, open on mobile viewport, verify menu opens and closes by tapping overlay

## Success Criteria
- [ ] SVG element has aria-hidden="true" attribute
- [ ] Overlay label exists with fixed inset-0, hidden by default, shown via peer-checked:block
- [ ] Overlay has aria-hidden="true" (it's a click target, not semantic content)
- [ ] Nav ul has z-index above the overlay
- [ ] Updated build test verifies aria-hidden presence
- [ ] All 22+ tests pass

## Key Considerations (SRE Review)

**Peer CSS Ordering**:
- The overlay label MUST come after the checkbox input and its sibling label, but before the ul
- Tailwind's peer modifier matches the first preceding sibling with the peer class
- The overlay uses peer-checked:block which references the #nav-toggle checkbox
- Order matters: input.peer -> label (hamburger) -> label (overlay) -> ul

**Z-Index Stacking**:
- Overlay: z-10 (covers page content)
- Nav menu: z-20 (renders above overlay)
- Without z-index, the nav menu could render behind the overlay

**Accessibility**:
- The overlay label has aria-hidden="true" because it's purely a UI mechanism
- Screen readers already have the checkbox toggle via the hamburger label's aria-label
- The overlay's for="nav-toggle" attribute makes it functional: clicking unchecks the checkbox

## Anti-patterns
- Do NOT use JavaScript for the overlay (CSS-only approach is cleaner and matches existing pattern)
- Do NOT remove the existing aria-label="Toggle navigation" from the hamburger label
- Do NOT make the overlay a div (must be a label with for= to toggle the checkbox)
